THE PRODUCT. The second half of the double-booking guarantee, and the half that may not be waived at any confidence for any reason (waiving a quality check is reserved to the client, CONSTITUTION Art III.8). TOTAL, NOT PARTIAL — the documents settle this explicitly and in five places. FR-ADR-024: 'The constraint is total, not partial. No WHERE status <> cancelled clause.' P-PAY-11: 'The constraint is total, not partial. There is no WHERE status <> cancelled clause, because P-PAY-12 rules out cancellation in v1. If cancellation is ever added, this constraint has to be revisited first — a cancelled booking holding a seat forever is what a total constraint would then produce.' Three criteria assert the absence of a WHERE clause directly against the catalogue: S-XCT-02 and S-XCT-03 read pg_get_constraintdef and require no WHERE; S-XCT-04 requires `SELECT indexdef FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = 'booking_seat'` to contain no WHERE and requires the guard to be a CONSTRAINT rather than a partial index; S-PAY-09 requires pg_indexes to return EXACTLY ONE unique index on this table. So a cancelled booking's seats are NOT freed, and that is the ruled behaviour, not an oversight. It must be created in the SAME Alembic revision as create_table('booking_seat') (S-XCT-04), so no window exists in which a seat row can be written without it, and no later revision may drop it.

column7: THE CHECK AND THE ACT IN ONE STATEMENT. The row is inserted FIRST, in the same transaction as the booking, before any other work. The insert either succeeds — this request owns the key — or it violates the constraint, in which case this request is a duplicate. There is no check-then-act window, which is exactly the trap GOTCHAS.md records: 'An idempotency key stored after the work is done is not idempotent. The three duplicate behaviours are the whole set: winner completed -> replay the stored response_body with the original status code; winner in_progress -> 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT with Retry-After (never a wait, because holding a connection open ties up one of ~110 on a db.t3.micro); fingerprint differs -> 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.

NOT NULL on every row without exception: a manager account with no usable password carries a real bcrypt digest of 32 discarded CSPRNG bytes, drawn PER ROW so two such rows never share a value (S-ACC-02 asserts count(*) - count(DISTINCT password_hash) = 0 over rows with last_signed_in_at IS NULL). A nullable column is refused by name, because a null test before the verification is the early return P-ACC-03's timing property forbids.

column7: NULL means the account has never signed in — a real and expected state, not a defect. NOT written on a failed attempt. `has_signed_in` on EP-ADM-22 is DERIVED as `last_signed_in_at IS NOT NULL` and is never stored (S-ADM-18 asserts no `has_signed_in` column exists in information_schema).
